findings.description: [defect] Single-column desktop layout leaves wide unused side margins and pushes the Selected Specification Details panel far below the fold (00-desktop-top.png, 01-desktop-full.png). All four sections are stacked in a narrow centered column (~60% of viewport width), separating the selected RFC-214 card at the top of the list from its detail view and action controls at the very bottom of the page instead of using the available horizontal space for a master-detail layout.

[defect] Flat, repetitive vertical stack with no visual differentiation across items or sections (00-desktop-top.png, 01-desktop-full.png). Every top-level section uses an identical bordered box, and all seven Specification List cards share the exact same rectangular shape and three-line gray prose template. High-risk P0 specs needing review (e.g., RFC-214 at 91/100) look visually identical to low-risk P2 approved specs (e.g., RFC-198 at 18/100) apart from the subtle selection fill/border, hindering queue triage.

[defect] Poor scannability and visual hierarchy caused by serializing structured operational data as plain prose (00-desktop-top.png, 01-desktop-full.png, 02-mobile-top.png). Queue Summary buries seven key metrics in a dense paragraph (three lines on desktop, eight lines on mobile), each specification item repeats full-sentence prose instead of aligned metadata or badges, and Selected Specification Details presents key attributes as flat pipe-delimited text lines.

[spec-mismatch] Inconsistent status label formatting across the page (00-desktop-top.png, 01-desktop-full.png). The Filter and Search Specifications buttons use human-readable Title Case labels ("Needs Review", "Changes Requested", "Approved"), whereas every Specification List card and the Selected Specification Details panel expose raw hyphenated lowercase slugs ("needs-review", "changes-requested", "approved") alongside unformatted ISO-8601 timestamps (e.g., "2026-11-27T08:30:00Z").

[defect] Header brand block is misaligned with the main content column's left key line (00-desktop-top.png, 01-desktop-full.png, 02-mobile-top.png). On desktop, the dark "F" logo extends slightly to the left of the left border of the cards below; on mobile, the logo aligns with neither the outer card border nor the inner card text axis.

[defect] Weak action hierarchy in Selected Specification Details (01-desktop-full.png). The primary decision buttons ("Approve Spec" and "Request Changes") use identical plain white bordered styling with no semantic emphasis and closely resemble inactive filter buttons, while the review checklist and history timeline rely on unstyled default checkboxes and plain bullet lists.

[defect] Mobile initial viewport is crowded by stacked summary prose and unevenly wrapped filter buttons (02-mobile-top.png). The four filter buttons wrap into two uneven rows with ragged right edges, and the combined height of the wrapped header, eight-line Queue Summary paragraph, and filter card leaves only the title and top line of RFC-214 visible at the bottom of the screen.

verdict.summary: The Fieldnote Spec Review Workbench renders without overlap or clipping, but has major layout, repetition, and hierarchy defects: on desktop it confines a master-detail workbench to a narrow single-column stack that pushes the selected specification details far below the fold, displays all seven specifications as identical plain-prose boxes with no visual encoding for status/priority/risk, and buries summary KPIs in dense paragraphs. Minor alignment, inconsistent raw status slug formatting, and flat button hierarchy issues further degrade usability.
